text: Evaluating a right coaction gives an action on the scalar extension A⊗V, as in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). Here the Hopf hypothesis makes every point invertible, so the construction packages these operators as A-linear automorphisms. Multiplication of points is convolution; multiplication of automorphisms is composition. No finite-dimensionality is assumed. Checks pass: [pointsAction_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/PointsAction/Basic.lean#L81), [endOfPoint_inv_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L519).
The automorphism has exactly the evaluated coaction as underlying linear map.
The inverse point cancels the evaluated operator.

The constructed automorphism has precisely the operator obtained by applying the point to the coaction coefficients. This equation ensures that packaging an invertible operator has not changed its action on A⊗V. It matches the evaluation construction in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95); invertibility comes from the Hopf structure, rather than from matrix determinants. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L119), [endOfPoint_comp_inv](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L525).
Pure-tensor evaluation identifies the actual operator.
The evaluated inverse point supplies the other inverse identity.

For an R-valued point, identify R⊗V with V by r⊗v↦rv. Conjugating the scalar-extended action through this identification gives the usual action on V from [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The stored representation preserves convolution multiplication and identity; its actual hypotheses include a Hopf algebra, without a finite-dimensionality assumption. Checks pass: [basePointsRepresentation_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/PointsAction/Basic.lean#L109), [basePointsRepresentation_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/PointsAction/Basic.lean#L119).
The transported action evaluates on 1⊗v then applies the tensor-unit identification.
Actual subcomodules are stable under the transported action.

This formula makes the transported base-point action explicit: apply the evaluated coaction to 1⊗v, then identify R⊗V with V. Thus its value is the sum of coaction vectors multiplied by their evaluated coefficients, exactly the right-coaction convention of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The tensor-unit identification involves ordinary scalar multiplication. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L119), [endOfPoint_one_tmul_eq_one_tmul_basePointsRepresentation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/PointsAction/Basic.lean#L134).
Pure-tensor evaluation gives the coefficient formula.
The scalar-extended action recovers the transported base action on 1⊗v.

Given a right coaction ρ:V→V⊗H, evaluate its H-coefficients at g:H→A and extend A-linearly. Thus a⊗v maps to Σ a g(v₁)⊗v₀, matching [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). Construction of this individual operator needs only the separate algebra and coalgebra structures; bialgebra compatibility is needed later for multiplication laws. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L119), [endOfPoint_tmul_of_coact_eq_tmul_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L125).
The actual defining operator has the expected pure-tensor formula.
A vector with coaction v⊗1 is fixed by every algebra-valued point.

On a pure tensor a⊗v, evaluation applies g to the coefficient factor of ρ(v), swaps factors to A⊗V, and multiplies by a. This is the basis-free version of the coefficient matrix evaluation in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The tensor swap only reorders factors; it does not assert that V embeds in its scalar extension. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tmul_of_coact_eq_tmul_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L125), [endOfPoint_groupLike](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L275).
The formula specializes correctly to a fixed vector.
The formula specializes to scalar multiplication for a group-like coaction.

If the coaction of v is v⊗1, every point fixes every a⊗v because an algebra homomorphism sends 1 to 1. This is the direct fixed-vector implication of the evaluation construction in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The statement assumes the coaction equality itself; it needs no density of rational points or reducedness hypothesis. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L119), [endOfPoint_trivial](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L574).
Evaluation on a pure tensor proves the forward fixed-vector implication.
For the trivial coaction the same conclusion holds on the whole module.

Changing coefficient algebra along φ:A→A′ commutes with evaluating a coaction: evaluating at φ∘g equals applying φ to the coefficients after evaluation at g. This is naturality of the algebra-valued points construction in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). Both composites are compared as R-linear maps, so neither injectivity of φ nor flatness is required. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L119), [endOfPoint_one_tmul_eq_one_tmul_basePointsRepresentation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/PointsAction/Basic.lean#L134).
Pure-tensor evaluation checks the coefficient-change square.
The base-valued specialization agrees with the ordinary representation.

A comodule morphism commutes with coactions, so its scalar extension intertwines every evaluated point operator. This is the morphism compatibility in [Milne, §9a compatibility laws](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). The displayed square compares A-linear maps between A⊗V and A⊗W; the morphism need not be injective or invertible, and no flatness is needed for this equality. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L119), [baseChange_comp_endOfPoint_regular](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L537).
Evaluation on pure tensors identifies both composites.
Regular comodules satisfy the corresponding bialgebra-map intertwining formula.

An injective comodule map preserves and reflects equality between a scalar-extended submodule and its image under a point operator. Flatness of A keeps the extended map injective, the principle in [Stacks, Lemma 10.39.5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9); intertwining then permits cancellation of submodule images. This is equality of submodule images, not merely forward invariance or a scheme-stabilizer theorem. Checks pass: [baseChange_comp_endOfPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L164), [basePointsRepresentation_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/PointsAction/Basic.lean#L119).
The extended comodule morphism intertwines the operators used in the image comparison.
Actual subcomodules give a native stable-subspace control.

Corestricting a coaction along a bialgebra map φ replaces ρ by (id⊗φ)ρ. Evaluating the new coaction at g therefore gives the original action evaluated at g∘φ. This is functorial coefficient evaluation as in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The underlying module is unchanged, and the map φ need not be injective or surjective. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L119), [basePointsRepresentation_corestrict](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/PointsAction/Basic.lean#L178).
Pure-tensor evaluation verifies the composite-coefficient formula.
The same pullback formula holds for the transported base-point representation.

For the coaction v↦v⊗x attached to a group-like element x of H, evaluation at g acts by the scalar g(x). This follows directly from [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95) and the explicitly selected group-like coaction. Group-like elements of H are coefficients, whereas points are algebra maps H→A; without Hopf hypotheses the scalar need not be a unit. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L119), [endOfPoint_trivial](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L574).
Evaluation gives g(x) times each pure tensor.
The group-like element 1 specializes to the identity operator.

Under the explicit hypothesis that the coaction on V⊗W is diagonal, a point acts separately on both tensor factors, as required in [Milne, §9a compatibility laws](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). The comparison identifies (a⊗v)⊗(b⊗w) with ab⊗(v⊗w). Multiplicativity of g evaluates the product of coaction coefficients; an arbitrary unrelated coaction would not satisfy this formula. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tensor_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L351), [endOfPoint_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L119).
The deliberately selected diagonal tensor comodule realizes the hypothesis.
Evaluation of the individual factors supplies the coefficient calculation.

The point operator on a diagonal tensor comodule is the tensor product of the two point operators, transported through the scalar-extension comparison. This is the tensor compatibility of [Milne, §9a compatibility laws](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). The theorem explicitly assumes the diagonal coaction equality; equality on pure tensors extends to all tensors by linearity, without requiring bases or finite-dimensionality. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tensor_tmul_of_coact_eq](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L301), [endOfPoint_tensor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L359).
The asserted linear-map identity holds on pure tensors under the same coaction hypothesis.
The standard diagonal tensor comodule supplies the concrete specialization.

This specializes factorwise point evaluation to the explicitly chosen diagonal comodule on V⊗W. Its coaction multiplies the H-coefficients in their given order; g turns that product into multiplication in the commutative value algebra A. The resulting pure-tensor formula is the tensor compatibility in [Milne, §9a compatibility laws](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175), without assuming H commutative. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tensor_tmul_of_coact_eq](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L301), [tensor_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L465).
The general formula checks the required diagonal-coaction condition.
The chosen tensor comodule really has the diagonal coaction.

For the chosen diagonal tensor comodule, the scalar-extension comparison carries the point operator to the tensor product of the individual operators. This realizes [Milne, §9a compatibility laws](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175) as an equality of A-linear maps. Selecting this coaction matters: the underlying tensor module can carry other coactions, for which this identity is not asserted. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tensor_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L351), [tensor_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/TensorProduct.lean#L465).
Pure tensors satisfy the claimed comparison.
The actual selected comodule is diagonal, rather than an arbitrary coaction.

The identity point is the counit, and evaluating the coaction at that counit gives the identity operator by the comodule counit law. This is the identity part of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). Here 1 denotes convolution identity among algebra maps, not the constant function with value 1, which generally would not be an algebra homomorphism. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L119), [endOfPoint_trivial](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L574).
The pure-tensor formula reduces evaluation to the counit law.
Every point acts identically on the selected trivial comodule.

Evaluating at the convolution product g*h gives E_g∘E_h, so h acts first. Coassociativity of the right coaction and commutativity of the value algebra supply the coefficient calculation, matching the multiplication order in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). This already works for bialgebras: neither inverse points nor commutativity of H is assumed. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_convOne](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L370), [endOfPoint_inv_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L519).
The counit point supplies the identity action.
In the Hopf specialization, the same composition order gives inverse cancellation.

If g*h=1 and both point operators preserve a submodule, E_g maps that submodule onto itself: an element x has preimage E_h(x). This uses the action law of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95) and only the stated one-sided inverse relation. Forward preservation alone would give inclusion, while the extra hypothesis supplies the reverse inclusion. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_convMul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L426), [endOfPoint_convOne](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L370).
Composition with the h-operator evaluates the product g*h.
The assumed product 1 acts identically, proving the preimage calculation.

The evaluated coaction operators form a representation of the convolution monoid on A⊗V. The stored identity and multiplication proofs are precisely the counit and coassociativity consequences described in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). At this bialgebra stage, representation means a monoid homomorphism to linear endomorphisms; it does not assert that every operator is invertible. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_convOne](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L370), [endOfPoint_convMul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L426).
Evaluation preserves the convolution identity.
Evaluation preserves convolution multiplication in the correct composition order.

Applying the packaged representation to a point gives exactly its evaluated-coaction operator. This equation connects the abstract monoid-homomorphism interface to the explicit coefficient formula of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The wrapper uses convolution on algebra maps and composition on endomorphisms; at these bialgebra hypotheses, an action by automorphisms is not required. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L119), [endOfPoint_convMul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L426).
The representation therefore has the expected concrete coefficient formula.
The underlying operators obey the packaged multiplication law.

For a Hopf algebra, applying the inverse point after the point gives the identity linear operator. The point inverse comes from precomposing with the antipode, so this performs no division by coordinate values. The proof specializes the representation multiplication law of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95) to g⁻¹*g=1, using the counit identity. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_convMul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L426), [endOfPoint_convOne](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L370).
The two operators compose to evaluation of g⁻¹*g.
Evaluation of their identity product is the identity map.

Applying a point after its inverse also gives the identity on A⊗V. Together with the opposite cancellation formula, this supplies an actual linear automorphism, as in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The proof applies left cancellation to the inverse point and uses involutivity of group inversion; it does not assume the antipode itself is bijective. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_inv_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L519), [pointsAction_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/PointsAction/Basic.lean#L81).
Left cancellation applied to the inverse point proves the claimed side.
The packaged linear automorphism uses this same evaluated operator.

A bialgebra map f:H→K intertwines the regular point actions when the point g of K is pulled back to g∘f on H. Regular coaction is comultiplication, so preservation of comultiplication proves the formula. This is the regular instance of morphism compatibility in [Milne, §9a compatibility laws](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175); f need not be injective or invertible. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L119), [baseChange_comp_endOfPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L164).
Pure tensors reduce the comparison to preservation of comultiplication.
General comodule morphisms satisfy the corresponding intertwining law.

Every algebra-valued point acts identically on the explicitly chosen trivial comodule: its coaction is v↦v⊗1, and g(1)=1. This is the trivial-action compatibility from [Milne, §9a compatibility laws](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175), here for the entire chosen module. The statement selects the trivial coaction rather than claiming that every coaction on the same underlying module is trivial. Checks pass: [trivial_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Trivial.lean#L225), [endOfPoint_groupLike](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L275).
The selected trivial coaction has the required v⊗1 formula.
The general group-like formula specializes at x=1 to the identity.

This packages common real and complex scalar arithmetic: a complete normed field, real scalar embedding, conjugation, and real and imaginary coordinates with the usual modulus formula. The distinguished imaginary unit may be zero for the real case. The supplied order compares real parts only when imaginary parts agree. Compared with [Axler §§1A, 4, 6A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/RCLike/Basic.lean#L61).

The real numbers receive the shared real/complex structure with real part equal to the input, imaginary part zero, imaginary unit zero, and conjugation the identity. Thus the coordinate formulas reduce to ordinary real arithmetic and the norm is absolute value; this does not assert that zero squares to minus one. Compared with [Axler §§1A, 4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/RCLike/Basic.lean#L787).

This supplies only a function taking two elements to a scalar, together with inner-product notation. It assumes no vector-space structure, positivity, symmetry, or linearity. Those mathematical properties belong to the later inner-product classes; the name here denotes the operation without asserting the usual inner-product properties. Compared with [Axler Definition 6.2](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Defs.lean#L82).

The inner product is Hermitian, conjugate-linear in its first argument and linear in its second, with real diagonal equal to the existing seminorm squared. Unlike the usual positive-definite convention, zero seminorm need not force a zero vector. Completeness is not required; Axler uses the opposite complex-slot convention. Compared with [Axler §6A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Defs.lean#L110).

This describes a positive semidefinite Hermitian form on a real or complex vector space before choosing a seminorm. It is conjugate-linear in the first argument and linear in the second. Nonzero vectors may have zero self-product; no quotient, existing norm, or completeness assumption is built into this construction. Compared with [Clément–Martin §4.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.03618) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Defs.lean#L140).

This adds positive definiteness to a positive semidefinite Hermitian form: a vector with zero self-product must be zero. The resulting real or complex inner product needs no preexisting norm or completeness. Its first argument is conjugate-linear, whereas Axler chooses linearity there; the two conventions differ by swapping arguments. Compared with [Axler §6A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Defs.lean#L155).

A positive-definite Hermitian form gives the norm √Re⟨x,x⟩ and hence a normed additive group. The input to the square root is nonnegative, and Cauchy–Schwarz supplies the triangle inequality. Positive definiteness supplies separation; this constructs the norm topology rather than assuming an existing topology or completing the space. Compared with [Clément–Martin §4.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.03618) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Defs.lean#L473).

Starting with a positive semidefinite Hermitian form, this equips its associated seminormed space with the same inner product. The seminorm is √Re⟨x,x⟩. Despite the name, the input is the weaker pre-inner-product core: nonzero null vectors are allowed, and the construction neither quotients them out nor assumes completeness. Compared with [Clément–Martin §4.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.03618) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Defs.lean#L572).

A real scalar is embedded into the real/complex field using its real-algebra map. Its real coordinate is unchanged and its imaginary coordinate is zero; the map preserves arithmetic and is injective. For the real instance it is the identity, while for complex numbers it is the usual real-axis inclusion. Compared with [Axler §§1A, 4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/RCLike/Basic.lean#L98).

The squared modulus sends z to (Re z)²+(Im z)² in the real numbers. It preserves zero, one, and multiplication, but not addition: squaring the modulus of 1+1 gives 4, not 2. Its values are nonnegative and vanish exactly at zero, including in the real specialization. Compared with [Axler Chapter 4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/RCLike/Basic.lean#L407).

The nonnegative square root of the squared modulus equals the norm. This uses both the sum-of-squares formula and nonnegativity of a norm, so there is no choice of sign. For a real input it returns absolute value, including zero; Lean’s convention for square roots of negative numbers is never needed. Compared with [Axler Definition 4.2](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/RCLike/Basic.lean#L477).

The norm of a natural number embedded into a real/complex field equals the same real number. The two casts have different targets, and zero is included. This follows from the absolute-value norm on the real axis; it is not a claim about arbitrary normed fields such as p-adic fields. Compared with [Axler §§1A, 4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/RCLike/Basic.lean#L655).

Embedding a real number commutes with taking its multiplicative inverse. For nonzero input this is the usual reciprocal on the real axis. Lean also defines the inverse of zero to be zero in both fields, so the displayed identity needs no nonzero hypothesis; zero is not claimed to have a reciprocal. Compared with [Axler §1A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/RCLike/Basic.lean#L483).

Every scalar is recovered as its real part plus its imaginary part times the distinguished imaginary unit. Both coordinates are real numbers embedded back into the scalar field before combining them. In the real instance the imaginary part and distinguished unit are zero, so the same formula reduces to the identity. Compared with [Axler Definition 4.1](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/RCLike/Basic.lean#L118).

The norm squared is the real sum (Re z)²+(Im z)², the usual Euclidean modulus formula. The existing norm is constrained to satisfy this equality; the statement is not a formula for z² in the scalar field. For real z it reduces to |z|²=z², with no positivity assumption on z. Compared with [Axler Definition 4.2](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/RCLike/Basic.lean#L418).

A scalar is nonnegative exactly when its imaginary part is zero and its real part is nonnegative. This is the scoped partial order on real/complex scalars, not an ordering by magnitude: a nonreal complex number is incomparable with zero. Every norm is nonnegative, but that does not make its input nonnegative. Compared with [Axler §6A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/RCLike/Basic.lean#L842).

This asserts that the given normed field admits compatible real/complex scalar data, with exactly the same operations, norm and topology. It records existence, not a chosen coordinate system or equality of its underlying set with ℝ or ℂ. In particular, it does not permit replacing the norm by a merely equivalent one. Compared with [Axler §§1A, 4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/RCLike/Basic.lean#L1296).

Given existence of compatible real/complex scalar data, this chooses such data and installs it while retaining the original normed-field structure exactly. The choice supplies real and imaginary coordinates and conjugation; it is not presented as a unique coordinate choice. No norm, field operation, or topology is replaced by an equivalent alternative. Compared with [Axler §§1A, 4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/RCLike/Basic.lean#L1348).

A real/complex scalar structure witnesses that its underlying normed field admits such a compatible structure. The witness is the structure already present, so the field operations and norm agree literally. It proves existence without adding a coordinate choice or classifying arbitrary complete normed fields as real or complex. Compared with [Axler §§1A, 4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/RCLike/Basic.lean#L1299).

The star operation is exactly the conjugation used for real/complex scalars. It fixes the real part and negates the imaginary part; on real numbers it is the identity. The equation identifies two names for the same operation, not every scalar with its conjugate, and not conjugation with taking a multiplicative inverse. Compared with [Axler Chapter 4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/RCLike/Basic.lean#L383).
